name: hello
note: console output through kernel32 WriteFile

name: entry-exit-code
source: fn main() -> u64 { return 7; }
note: u64 main reaches ExitProcess with the return value

name: integer-print
note: checked integer arithmetic and decimal formatting

name: float-print
note: SSE scalar arithmetic and float formatting

name: file-write-read
note: CreateFileA/WriteFile/ReadFile/CloseHandle round trip

name: arguments
note: argv recovered from GetCommandLineA; the entry requires exactly one argument

name: struct-fields
note: aggregate layout and field access; x+y is the process exit code

name: argument-list
note: full argv list: count plus every argument after the program path

name: thread-join
note: CreateThread through the Win64 bridge, then a join that waits for thread termination

name: thread-wake
note: futex-equivalent wait/wake: FUTEX_WAIT -> WaitOnAddress, FUTEX_WAKE -> WakeByAddressSingle

name: com-interop
note: CoInitializeEx/CoUninitialize plus IUnknown through a C-ABI vtable shim; E_POINTER and E_NOINTERFACE are exact

name: ffi-call-abi
note: extern C on Win64: rcx/rdx/r8/r9 and positional xmm0-3, 32-byte shadow space, stack slots from the fifth argument, f32 as binary32, narrow results re-extended

name: ffi-out-params
note: extern C out-parameters on Win64: the slot address is the C H *, a null-initialized slot reads as zero, and the callee's write is visible to Grail; the out slot as a stack argument and as the last argument after a record pointer and a two-word view

name: ffi-record-pointers
note: records by pointer and record out-parameters on Win64: cptr(&r) is the struct address a create-info field holds, &mut R is the callee's T *, an array of handles crosses out and back and the handle Grail reads equals the one C wrote, and one count record across two declarations of one symbol exits without aborting

name: ffi-call-words
note: seven, eight and nine word arguments on Win64: four registers, a 32-byte home area, then stack slots, with the same position-weighted sums as the ELF targets

name: ffi-dynamic-loading
note: LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress/FreeLibrary through extern declarations imported per symbol; cfn values called with Win64; ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND for a missing DLL

name: io-error-mapping
stdout:
not found

ok
directory not empty
ok

note: Win32 GetLastError codes map to the errno values io::Error understands (ENOENT, ENOTDIR, ENOTEMPTY, ...)

name: ffi-call-records
note: Win64 record results: 8 bytes in rax, 16 and 24 bytes through a hidden pointer in rcx

name: ffi-call-variadic
note: Win64 variadics: doubles passed in both the xmm and the integer register of their slot

name: ffi-com-slot
note: COM-shaped vtable method with seven arguments (three on the stack) and float slots, called through a cfn

name: ffi-float-records
note: f32/f64 fields at C offsets in a viewport-shaped record

name: ffi-callback-floats
note: Win64 callbacks: positional xmm parameters, a float on the stack, narrow integers extended by the callee

name: ffi-float-record-results
note: Win64 classifies record results by size only: 8-byte records in rax, others through a hidden pointer

name: tasks-scope-and-parallel-map
note: spawn/task_scope/parallel_map on the green scheduler: fibers on one scheduler thread, the same cooperative semantics Linux has

name: tasks-sleep-overlap
note: four sleeping tasks overlap: each parks the task and lets the others run (the sleep runs on a helper thread because Windows has no timerfd)

name: ffi-nested-records
note: extern records embedded by value at C offsets

name: tasks-interleave-at-yield
note: one scheduler thread, FIFO run queue: a task runs until it yields, so the two tasks alternate in a fixed order and neither is preempted mid-run. Not run as ELF: a Linux queue has a worker per CPU, where the order is deliberately free.

name: tasks-sleep-progress
note: a task parked in host::sleep_ms does not stop another task from making progress: the sleeper reads the word the other task wrote while it slept

name: tasks-read-file-offload
note: host::read_file from a task hands the blocking I/O to an offload thread and parks the task (rt_blocking_call/rt_offload), so another task runs while the file is being read, on Windows as on Linux

name: tasks-thread-mode
note: the opt-in thread-per-task scheduler (GRAIL_TASKS=thread) still runs: a task that never yields makes progress beside another because both own an OS thread; rt_task_threads() reports the mode as 1

name: command-with-env
note: CreateProcessA with an explicit environment block: FOO reaches the child

name: command-inherit-env
note: host::command passes a NULL environment block, so the child keeps this process's variables

name: command-empty-env
note: an explicit empty block replaces the environment; Wine still adds its own system variables, PATH is not one of them

name: command-argv-round-trip
note: the argument vector is quoted back into a command line: a spaced argument, a literal quote and a backslash reach the child unchanged

name: ffi-byval-records
note: Win64 byval: records of 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes in their positional integer slot (floats included), any other size by reference to a 16-byte-aligned caller copy; stack slots above the 32-byte home area

name: ffi-callback-stack
note: Win64 callbacks reading arguments past the sixth from the caller frame (208+8i(%rbp) in the body), narrow and f32 values among them

name: ffi-callback-record-write
note: a Win64 callback writing through p: &mut R: copy-in/copy-out on fall-through, early return and whole-value exchange

name: ffi-nested-float-results
note: record results with floats inside embedded records: Win64 returns by size (rax or a hidden pointer), Windows ARM64 classifies the flattened fields like AAPCS64
